the results show that the use of e learning has not been able to meet user satisfaction in terms of system quality, information quality, and service quality, due to various factors, including the user’s discomfort in accessing e learning, inaccuracy, and the lack of speed in the event of errors when using e learning.
the results of this study indicate that the use of e-learning systems can increase student satisfaction, but it is not enough to make students satisfied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DeLone and MacLean (2003) model is a useful framework for understanding how e-learning affects student satisfaction, which in turn affects student performance.
the DeLone & McLean Model is not a one size fits all solution for measuring user satisfaction.
, by using DeLone and Mclane’s model, we can measure the level of user satisfaction with the e-learning system, and then we can improve the system based on user satisfaction.
